claim: Let \(Q_3\) be the graph on \(\{0,1\}^3\) with edges joining binary strings at Hamming distance one, and let \(\mathcal M(Q_3)\) be its ordinary Morse complex of acyclic discrete vector fields. Then \[\widetilde H_i(\mathcal M(Q_3);\mathbb F_2)\cong \begin{cases}\mathbb F_2^4,&i=5,\\\mathbb F_2^{139},&i=6,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The nonempty face vector in dimensions \(0,\ldots,6\) is \((24,240,1296,4080,7488,7424,3072)\), and the augmented mod-\(2\) boundary ranks from dimensions \(0,\ldots,6\) are \((1,23,217,1079,3001,4487,2933)\).
integrity: The finite claim is reconstructed from the definition: all \(3^{12}\) edge states are independently checked, the face vector is cross-checked by the graph-Laplacian generating identity, every simplicial \(\partial^2\) check is replayed, and boundary ranks are recomputed by three exact mod-\(2\) elimination routes. The proof does not infer an infinite statement from finite experiments.
scientific_limitations: The result is restricted to reduced homology of \(\mathcal M(Q_3)\) with \(\mathbb F_2\) coefficients. It makes no integral-homology, torsion, cohomology-ring, full-homotopy-type, or higher-hypercube claim. A directed-forest thesis on Cayley graphs is a residual bibliographic risk because its full text was unavailable during comparison.
title: Mod-\(2\) homology of the cube-graph Morse complex is concentrated in degrees \(5\) and \(6\)
